title: 第14章
content_zh:
这四件事，是必问题，展颜每次的回答，也都大同小异。贺叔叔的声音，在电话里，又深沉，又温柔，展颜没被男性长辈这么细碎的关怀过，她以为，男人要么像爷爷爸爸那样沉闷，要么就像孙晚秋她爸，喜欢喝酒打人。
她觉得孤独，这里很好，可不是她的家。贺叔叔的声音，也只是短暂地抚平一下这种孤独。
每天记十五个英语单词，背两篇短文；看半小时新闻，了解国内外大事；预习高中课本，做数理化习题；最后，就是读报看杂志。
他从餐桌旁站起，打个手势，示意展颜不要急着挂，展颜便说：“哥哥有话要讲。”
打开的这页，密密麻麻写着价格传真，括号里有“北京中关村”字样。展颜往前翻了下，杂志叫《微型计算机》。
展颜心想，不知道要卖多少小麦玉米才能买一样啊。她偷瞥眼贺图南，发现他正闲散地靠桌旁跟贺叔叔说话，连忙在杂志上找刚才听到的菲利普索尼。
一亩地产出七八百斤，去掉交税，种子化肥农药，一季小麦，一季玉米，这是大头，再加上点儿大豆、棉花，一年到两头剩也就是一千出头，家里五口人，不按劳力，按人头算，一人一亩二三分土地，那么总收入就是……
“来，哥哥看你算什么呢？”贺图南不知什么时候绕到了背后，见她写数字，一把夺过纸，上头是些简单的加减乘除。
展颜想去夺，他个头高，恶劣地一扬手：“算花了多少钱？你还不清的。”
贺图南笑得漫不经心：“我不懂？”他大喇喇坐下，拈着这片纸，又扫了两眼，说，“以后就我们两个人时，你喊我名字就行，我不是你哥哥。”
他不知想起什么，神情变淡，把纸推给她，顺便把今早买的报纸也推给她。
乡下没人看报纸，电视里放新闻，大家就看，没电视的，夜里守着收音机在床头打盹，听着听着就睡着了。
贺叔叔爱看报，每次路过报刊亭，都要买一堆花花绿绿的报纸回来，展颜也跟着看，多了见识：有《沿海时报》，有《北京晨报》，有《经济日报》，还有《书报文摘》。
content_en:
These four things are necessary questions, and Zhanyan’s answers are similar every time. Uncle He's voice on the phone was deep and gentle. Zhan Yan had never received such detailed care from a male elder. She thought that men were either as boring as her grandfather and father, or like Sun Wanqiu's father, who liked to drink and beat people.
She felt lonely, it was nice here, but it wasn't her home. Uncle He's voice only temporarily soothed this loneliness.
Memorize fifteen English words and memorize two short articles every day; watch the news for half an hour to understand major domestic and international events; preview high school textbooks and do math, physics and chemistry exercises; finally, read newspapers and magazines.
He stood up from the dining table and gestured to Zhanyan not to worry, and Zhanyan said, "Brother has something to say."
The page that opened was densely written with price faxes, with the words "Beijing Zhongguancun" in brackets. Zhanyan flipped forward and saw that the magazine was called "Microcomputer".
Zhanyan thought to himself, I wonder how much wheat and corn I have to sell to buy the same thing. She stole a glance at He Tunan and found that he was talking idly to Uncle He at the table. She quickly looked for the Philip Soni she had just heard in the magazine.
One acre of land produces 700 to 800 kilograms. Excluding taxes, seeds, fertilizers and pesticides, one season of wheat, one season of corn, which is the bulk, plus some soybeans and cotton, the remaining output is just over a thousand pounds a year. If there are five people in the family, not based on labor, but based on head count, one person has one acre and two-thirds of land, so the total income is...
"Come on, brother, who do you think you are?" He Tunan came around from behind at some point and saw her writing numbers. He grabbed the paper and found some simple addition, subtraction, multiplication and division on it.
Zhan Yan wanted to snatch it away, but he was tall and raised his hand in a bad way: "How much did it cost? You can't even pay it back."
He Tunan smiled carelessly: "I don't understand?" He sat down, held the piece of paper, glanced at it twice, and said, "From now on, when it's just the two of us, just call me by my name. I'm not your brother."
He didn't know what he thought of, his expression became pale, and he pushed the paper to her, along with the newspaper he bought this morning.
In the countryside, no one reads newspapers. Everyone watches the news when it is on TV. Those who don’t have a TV doze at the bedside with the radio in front of them, and fall asleep while listening to it.
Uncle He loved to read newspapers. Every time he passed by a newsstand, he would buy a bunch of colorful newspapers. Zhanyan also read them and gained more knowledge: there were "Coastal Times", "Beijing Morning News", "Economic Daily", and "Books and Newspapers Digest".
